admission.justification: The four boundaries determine later transaction and history changes; treating the formerly catalogued limits as bugs was rejected in favor of preserving their specific attribution, approval, input and timeline reasons.

alternatives.option: Retain the four designs together with exact-pair admission at every landing.
alternatives.reason: Code attribution needs the already-existing code commit; failed claims cannot reliably be released; judgment holds only for current inputs; frozen publication history retains prior change decisions without letting fabricated history replace them.

alternatives.option: Treat the four retained boundaries as accepted limits to remove or work around.
alternatives.reason: The requirement identifies them as designs with reasons, not exemptions from landing judgment. Removing them would lose code attribution, invent approval recovery, reuse stale verdicts or overwrite durable judgment history.
alternatives.reconsider_when: An approved redesign changes attribution, approval-claim authority or frozen-history ownership while preserving exact judged publication.

consequences: Code is committed before memory because the memory commit names its code commit in its trailer; the leaf's own branch is not a landing line until closeout completes and rule 3 guards the landing.
An approval covers one attempt because releasing a claim after a failure cannot be guaranteed; the gate preflight runs before the claim so a gate refusal costs no approval.
A recovered closeout is judged against the parent line as it is now because a verdict holds only for the inputs it read.

A change already on the parent line may be answered by any later row, and a changed family row keeps its disposition in a later attempt of the same leaf; the changed row stays frozen in the landed history and the record timeline while rule 5 blocks replacement.
context: The packet distinguishes four retained transaction/history designs from bypasses to repair: code/memory order, approval claim lifetime, input-bound recovery and parent-line history.
